issues.legal_issue: A child of the husband from whom a female seller inherited property is entitled to pre-emption when she sells that property, even if the child is not her own offspring.
material_facts: The female seller had inherited the land through her husband and later sold it.
The claimant was the daughter of that husband by another wife.
issues.conclusion: The claimant had a right of pre-emption under the first paragraph of clause (b) of section 15(2), even before the 1964 amendment.
issues.legal_principle: Section 15(2)(b) of the Punjab Pre-emption Act, 1913, gives the first right of pre-emption to the son or daughter of the husband through whom the female seller inherited the property; this includes that husband's child by another wife. The scheme of section 15(2) confines the right to the lineal descendants of the last male holder. The Court relied on Mota Singh v. Prem Parkash Kaur for the principle that the property should not pass outside the line of the last male holder.

predicates.preemption_proceeding: The dispute concerns a claim to obtain property by exercising a right of pre-emption.
predicates.female_sold_property_inherited_through_h: A female seller sold property that she had inherited through her husband.
predicates.claimant_is_child_of_inheriting_husband: The person claiming pre-emption was a child of the husband through whom the seller inherited the property, whether or not the child was born to the seller.
predicates.claimant_has_preemption_right: The claimant is entitled to exercise the right of pre-emption over the property.

issues.definition: When a pre-emption claim concerns property a female seller inherited through her husband, a child of that husband is entitled to pre-emption even if the child was not born to the seller.

issues.legal_issue: A clarifying amendment to the law of pre-emption applies retrospectively to pending proceedings even without express language giving it retrospective effect.
material_facts: The claimant's pre-emption suit and subsequent appeals were pending when the 1964 amendment was enacted.
The amendment inserted words clarifying that the relevant children were those of the husband through whom the female seller had inherited the property.
The Court concluded that the claimant was entitled to pre-emption under the law even before the amendment.
issues.conclusion: The 1964 amendment was clarificatory or declaratory and had retrospective effect, so it applied to the pending proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: A curative or declaratory amendment that clarifies the previous law is more readily given retrospective effect than legislation that prejudicially affects past rights and transactions. Section 31, inserted by the 1960 amendment, applied to that amendment and did not itself extend to later amendments. The Court relied on Ram Sarup v. Munshi for the scope of section 31 and on Moti Ram v. Bakhwant Singh for retrospective treatment of a clarifying amendment.

predicates.preemption_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a claim to obtain property by exercising a right of pre-emption.
predicates.proceeding_pending_when_clarifying_amend: The dispute was still pending when the amendment was enacted.
predicates.amendment_clarifies_existing_law: The amendment clarifies the meaning of the law as it stood before the amendment.
predicates.amendment_applies_retroactively: The amendment governs the pending dispute as well as disputes arising after its enactment.

issues.definition: A clarifying amendment applies to a pending pre-emption proceeding when it was enacted while the proceeding was pending and clarifies the law that already existed.
